alex: Heads-up — saw a weird pattern when we switched KV cache to INT8 on the 4xA100 pool: memory drops ~35% as expected but p99 decode latency jumps and some long-context samples hallucinate token repeats. Anyone seen similar?

maria: likely kernel-selection fallout. Did the runtime pick the new low-bit KV matmul kernel?

alex: yes, runtime selected `matmul_kern_v2_int8_fast` automatically. config: `kv_quant_mode=INT8, kernel_autoselect=auto, seq_threshold=1024`.

tj: can you paste perf numbers? p50/p95/p99 and mem usage?

alex: quick paste from perf-run:v3
```
config: kv=INT8, model=titan-8b, batch=1, seq=2048
mem: 6.2GB (was 9.5GB in FP16)
latency: p50=52ms p95=120ms p99=380ms (FP16: p99=210ms)
error: decode divergence on 3/200 eval prompts -> repeated trigram loops
```

maria: interesting — memory improvement good, but p99 regression and quality issues. Could be quantization scale instability during autoregressive KV updates. INT8 KV accumulators sometimes lose dynamic range on long recency windows.

jia: we hit similar once with FP8 KVs + fused-kernel. Two suggestions: 1) run per-layer calibration with running-range (min/max) instead of static per-weight; 2) try hybrid key: INT8 keys + FP16 values (or vice versa) to keep decode stable.
dave: +1 on hybrid. Also consider batching heuristics: continuous batching might increase KV reuse and exacerbate scale drift if kernels assume independent streams. Try `batching.window_ms=0` to force immediate dispatch for a quick test.

tj: small repro script to compare variants quickly:
```
for mode in FP16 INT8 INT8-hybrid FP8; do
  ./tools/bench_decode --model titan-8b --kv-mode $mode --seq 2048 --runs 100 --dump-stats $mode.json
done
```

alex: ran that overnight. quick aggregated results:
```
FP16: mem=9.5GB, p99=210ms, qual=baseline
INT8: mem=6.2GB, p99=380ms, qual=-2.3% BLEU-ish proxy
INT8-hybrid: mem=7.9GB, p99=230ms, qual=-0.3%
FP8: mem=5.8GB, p99=410ms, qual=-4.5%
```

maria: hybrid looks promising — small mem trade for almost baseline quality and latency. Do we know why INT8 pure regresses latency? My guess: fallback paths in kernel (dequant/requant) create extra ops on decode that the scheduler isn't coalescing. Need kernel-level trace.

jia: I captured a short nvprof trace. Key spot is repeated `requantize_kv` calls at each decode step, adding ~8us per token but at long seq they pile up causing p99 tail. Also noticed quant scale recalibration calls (sync ops) every ~128 decode steps.

dave: that sync op is probably from our calibration auto-tuner. Can we disable auto-recalib during decode? maybe run offline calibration once per rollout instead of runtime adjustments.

alex: quick experiment: disable runtime-recalib -> p99 drops from 380ms to 225ms on INT8 but quality still off.

tj: so two issues: (1) runtime recalib causes tail latency, (2) pure INT8 loses numeric fidelity. For (1) we should gate recalib behind low-qps or background thread and make it non-blocking. For (2) hybrid or per-layer FP16 values seems best.

maria: agree. Action items:
- implement non-blocking calib candidate (jia + eng-runtime)
- add hybrid KV kernel variant and expose `kv_value_precision` flag (alex + tj)
- add telemetry for `requantize_kv` op counts and per-token extra-us contrib (observability) (dave + eng-sre)
- quick rollout plan: canary hybrid on 10% of traffic, monitor p99 and model-quality eval set

jia: I'll attach nvprof snippet and suggested patch to skip calib sync when `--kv-runtime-calib=off` in a follow-up thread.

sre-bot: deploy 1778000780 -> eng-runtime/kv-int8-hotfix started by alex :rocket:

dave: one more note — for safety, add an automatic fallback policy: if p99 > 300ms OR quality delta < -1.0% on eval set for 5 minutes, route to FP16 pool automatically. Keeps sites safe during unexpected quant regressions.

alex: thanks team. I'll start on the hybrid kernel PR and can run the 10% canary next week. Will post results here. :thumbsup:
